title: Bounded search for a fixed-length extension
statement: Let $Q,e,c_V,c_I$ be natural numbers, let $V$ be a language of Boolean words, and let $M_V,M_I,M_P$ be finite-state Boolean Turing machines. Suppose the clean simulation of $M_V$, started in its initial state on any Boolean word $y$, halts with output equal to the indicator of whether $y\in V$, clears all work tapes and returns all work-tape heads to the origin, and throughout the run keeps every work-tape head within distance $c_V(|y|^e+1)$ of the origin. Suppose also that $M_I$ computes the identity on every Boolean word of length $n$ in time $c_I(n+1)$, and that its space use on every input at every time is at most $c_I$. Then, on every Boolean input $x$, the specified search machine, started with its loop state, a false word of length $Q$ on its first work tape, and a true word of length $Q$ on its last work tape, halts with output indicating whether there is a word $u$ of length $Q$ such that the concatenation of $x$ and $u$ belongs to $V$. At every time up to and including that halting time, each work-tape head stays within distance $|x|+Q+c_V((|x|+Q)^e+1)+c_I+1$ of the origin.
